title: Potato, boiled, fresh, peel eaten, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Boiled potato is a whole tuber cooked in water without added fat. The peel is retained, preserving most of the dietary fiber, vitamins, and minerals. Potato is a staple food in many countries and is often used as a side dish or a base for other meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes were introduced to Europe from South America in the 16th century and quickly became a major food source.
The peel of boiled potatoes contains more fiber, vitamin C, and potassium than the flesh alone.
Boiled potatoes are easily digestible and are often recommended in diets aimed at gastrointestinal recovery.
There are over 4,000 potato varieties, differing in skin color, taste, and starch content.
Boiled potatoes can be used as a base for mash, salads, soups, and casseroles.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C in the peel and flesh supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion, promotes satiety, and supports gut microbiota.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Starch in boiled potatoes provides a steady release of energy.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Boiled potatoes have a high glycemic index, which can cause rapid blood sugar spikes in people with diabetes.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: If tubers are damaged or sprouting, the peel may contain solanine, a toxic compound. Green areas should be removed.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergy to potatoes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled potatoes can be served whole, diced into salads, mashed without butter, or used in casseroles and soups. The peel can be eaten together with the flesh, especially when it is well‑washed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store boiled potatoes in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 3–4 days. Do not leave them at room temperature for more than two hours to prevent bacterial growth.
